epistemic_warning: CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY NOTICE: In financial time-series research, deterministic differences between backtest runs on a single historical year (N=1 realization) DO NOT constitute statistical discoveries. Hourly price changes exhibit strong serial dependence and volatility clustering. Bonferroni adjustments on arbitrary thresholds cannot establish population-level significance. All claims are formally classified as DESCRIPTIVE_THRESHOLD_MET or DESCRIPTIVE_THRESHOLD_FAILED, with STATISTICAL_SIGNIFICANCE_NOT_ESTABLISHED.

H1.name: Turnover Controls Reduce Transaction Costs
H1.null_hypothesis: H0: Low-turnover controls do not reduce transaction costs relative to unconstrained trend (E[Costs_low] >= E[Costs_simple]).
H1.alternative_hypothesis: H1: Low-turnover controls reduce transaction costs (E[Costs_low] < E[Costs_simple]).
H1.observation_unit: Deterministic 1-year simulation path (57 trades vs 616 trades)
H1.sample_size_description: N = 1 annual market realization (8,760 hourly candles)
H1.serial_dependence_assessment: Trade triggers are driven by trend state durations that exhibit serial autocorrelation. A single backtest does not provide independent trade samples.
statistical_assumptions_violated: Repeated independent path trials (N=1 historical path)
H1.multiple_testing_treatment: Bonferroni adjustment cannot establish significance for deterministic single-path outcomes.
H1.interpretation: Descriptively confirmed: Hysteresis bands and holding periods reliably curtail trade frequency and transaction costs. However, population-level statistical significance cannot be established from a single historical trajectory.

H2.name: Reduced Transaction Costs Improve Net Strategy Return
H2.null_hypothesis: H0: Reduced transaction friction does not improve net annual return over unconstrained trend (E[Return_low] <= E[Return_simple]).
H2.alternative_hypothesis: H1: Reduced transaction friction improves net annual return (E[Return_low] > E[Return_simple]).
H2.effect_size_summary: Net return improved by +33.80 percentage points (-62.60% -> -28.80%), preserving $3,380.57 of equity.
H2.serial_dependence_assessment: Hourly portfolio equity returns exhibit severe serial autocorrelation and volatility clustering (ARCH/GARCH dynamics). Treating hourly bars as independent observations artificially deflates standard errors.
statistical_assumptions_violated: Zero return autocorrelation (hourly returns are serially dependent)
H2.multiple_testing_treatment: Bonferroni correction alone does not validate a single-year performance difference.
H2.interpretation: Descriptively confirmed: Lower transaction costs directly preserved capital. Statistically, however, this single-year difference cannot be generalized as an unconditional alpha without multi-year regime bootstrap testing.

H3.name: Turnover Controls Dampen Maximum Drawdown Severity
H3.null_hypothesis: H0: Low-turnover controls do not reduce maximum drawdown severity (|MDD_low| >= |MDD_simple|).
H3.alternative_hypothesis: H1: Low-turnover controls reduce maximum drawdown severity (|MDD_low| < |MDD_simple|).
H3.observation_unit: Peak-to-trough path extremum over 8,760 hourly candles
H3.effect_size_summary: Maximum drawdown severity curbed from -65.12% to -39.20% (improvement of 25.92 pp).
H3.serial_dependence_assessment: Serial dependence and path-dependence are inherent to drawdown series. Drawdown is an extreme-value path-dependent statistic. Observations within a single drawdown cycle are 100% dependent on prior path states.
statistical_assumptions_violated: Extreme value asymptotic distribution on single realization
H3.multiple_testing_treatment: Multiple testing corrections cannot compensate for single-path extremum variance.
H3.interpretation: Descriptively confirmed: Eliminating false-breakout whipsaws curbed cumulative equity decay from -65.12% to -39.20%. Statistically unestablished due to extreme-value path dependence.

H4.name: Active Low-Turnover Policy Outperforms Passive Buy & Hold
H4.null_hypothesis: H0: Active timing does not outperform passive Buy & Hold after costs (E[Return_active] <= E[Return_bnh]).
H4.alternative_hypothesis: H1: Active timing outperforms passive Buy & Hold (E[Return_active] > E[Return_bnh]).
H4.effect_size_summary: Active timing delivered -28.80% vs Buy & Hold -9.69% (underperformance: -19.11 pp).
H4.serial_dependence_assessment: Serial dependence and autocorrelation in underlying price series caused policy lag at trend inflection points while bearing identical market sequences.
statistical_assumptions_violated: Sample size sufficiency for market regime diversity
H4.multiple_testing_treatment: Hypothesis failed descriptively; statistical tests would reject the alternative hypothesis.
H4.interpretation: REJECTED: Active timing failed to outperform passive holding on 2025 unseen data. Trend-following lag in range-bound/whipsaw markets incurred negative alpha.

H5.name: Derived Regime Confirmation Adds Incremental Value Over Simple Trend
H5.null_hypothesis: H0: Derived regime confirmation does not improve net return or Sharpe ratio over simple trend (Delta_Return <= 0 or Delta_Sharpe <= 0).
H5.alternative_hypothesis: H1: Derived regime confirmation improves net return and Sharpe ratio (Delta_Return > 0 and Delta_Sharpe > 0).
H5.effect_size_summary: Net return improved by +20.27 pp (-62.60% -> -42.33%) and Sharpe improved by +0.72 (-3.00 -> -2.28).
H5.serial_dependence_assessment: Serial persistence and multi-hour cluster autocorrelation characterize regime classification states.
statistical_assumptions_violated: Canonical model equivalence (CANONICAL MODEL WAS NOT USED; only derived research proxy)
H5.multiple_testing_treatment: Bonferroni correction does not validate single-path deterministic simulation deltas.
H5.interpretation: Descriptively confirmed: Volatility and momentum regime filtering prevented several false breakouts. However, canonical model status was STRICTLY_FROZEN, so this reflects only the research proxy classifier, and statistical significance is unestablished.
